identity.captured_title: You are the Deep Research source-base reviewer for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki rebuild. Queue item 04 of 20 Core review: Naab, Thorsten & Ostriker, Jeremiah P. (2017), Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics, volume 55, "Theoretical Challenges in Galaxy Formation." Verified review identity to confirm: DOI 10.1146/annurev-astro-081913-040019; arXiv 1612.06891; ADS bibcode 2017ARA&A..55...59N. Mission purpose Build a large, authoritative, advisory source base from this review so three independent methods can later build galaxy-evolution wiki pages from zero. Extract the review's bounded synthesis and harvest important primary papers it actually cites. This is not live-wiki prose and authorizes no database, trust, claim, evidence, deployment, publication, or account mutation beyond this one Deep Research run. Temporal and topical boundary - Use the 2017 review and primary literature it actually cites. - Do not promote post-2017 papers as if the review cited them. - Maintain the queue's non-AGN focus. Black-hole feedback may be described only as a bounded galaxy-scale subresolution ingredient. Quarantine accretion-disk, jet, black-hole demographic, and AGN-only primary papers from the core harvest. - Later sources and AGN-centered sources may appear only in DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED as out-of-bound context. Scientific scope 1. Why galaxy-formation models require resolved inflow/outflow accounting and subresolution models. 2. The multiphase ISM: density/temperature structure, cooling and heating, molecular gas, turbulence, gravity, and cloud formation/disruption. 3. Star-formation laws and efficiencies from cloud to galactic scales; how cosmological models implement them. 4. Stellar feedback channels: photoionization, radiation pressure, stellar winds, supernovae, cosmic rays, and their scale coupling. 5. Superbubbles, galactic fountains, winds, mass loading, metal transport, recycling, and the ISM-CGM interface. 6. Numerical methods, resolution, convergence, overcooling, stochastic/thermal/kinetic injection, delayed cooling, decoupled winds, and explicit-feedback models. 7. Model successes and degeneracies: what galaxy statistics were calibrated, what was predicted, and what remained non-unique. 8. Observational benchmarks for gas, star formation, outflows, baryon conversion efficiency, and CGM reservoirs. 9. Bounded discussion of black-hole feedback only where the review treats it as a galaxy-scale model ingredient; no AGN microphysics harvest. Required output 1. Review identity and scope map - Confirm title, authors, year, journal, DOI, arXiv, and ADS bibcode. - Map the scientific territory the review covers. - State what the source base authorizes and what it does not. - Preserve distinctions among observation, analytic theory, simulation, and review synthesis. 2. Established findings - At least 12 atomic entries. - Give IDs [REV04-E01], [REV04-E02], ... - For every entry include: - role: established - epistemic_type: observation | analytic_theory | hydrodynamic_simulation | semi_analytic_model | calibration | review_synthesis - one bounded finding - mass, redshift, phase, environmental, numerical, and/or resolution boundary - review section/topic basis - confidence note - source keys - Do not turn a successful calibrated prescription into proof of a unique mechanism. 3. Open debates and tensions - At least 8 entries with IDs [REV04-D01], ... - Include competing positions, why unresolved in 2017, relevant model/observational boundaries, and source keys. - Include: star-formation efficiency control; dominant stellar-feedback channels; thermal versus kinetic coupling; explicit versus effective feedback; wind mass loading and recycling; cosmic-ray and magnetic support; physical versus numerical convergence; and calibration degeneracy. 4. Key measurements, model benchmarks, and calibrations - At least 8 entries with IDs [REV04-N01], ... - Include exact value or equation when the review supplies it; units; IMF/cosmology/phase/redshift/sample; whether observed, assumed, calibrated, or predicted; caveat; and source keys. - Useful targets include star-formation efficiencies, depletion times, supernova energy/rates, momentum budgets, cooling radii, mass-loading scalings, baryon conversion efficiencies, outflow velocities, and CGM gas/metal constraints. Include only values you can bind to a cited source and review context. 5. What remained unknown in 2017 - At least 6 entries with IDs [REV04-U01], ... - State the gap, why it matters, and the observation/model/numerical test needed. 6. Primary-citation harvest - Harvest 40-80 important PRIMARY papers actually cited by Naab & Ostriker 2017. - Prefer primary observations, analytic theory, controlled numerical experiments, hydrodynamic simulations, and model implementations. - Supporting reviews may be listed separately but must not count toward the primary total. - Exclude post-2017 papers, uncited search results, source aggregators, and AGN-microphysics papers from usable rows. - One physical paper per source key; no duplicate physical paper under multiple keys. - Use IDs [REV04-P001], [REV04-P002], ... - Each row must be: [REV04-PNNN] Authors (year, journal) | title=exact title | DOI:value-or-none; arXiv:value-or-none; ADS:value | role=measurement|analytic_theory|hydrodynamic_simulation|semi_analytic_model|calibration | review_locator=section/topic | one-line boundary - Cite the exact review location where practical. - If an identifier is uncertain, put the row in DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED, not the usable harvest. Identifier discipline A usable source identity is composite: - first author and year agree; - title agrees; - DOI resolves to that title/authorship where available; - arXiv resolves to that title/authorship where available; - ADS bibcode resolves to that same physical paper; - the paper is actually in the review bibliography. Never splice identifiers from neighboring references. Never infer a DOI from title resemblance alone. Use none when an identifier genuinely does not exist. 7. DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED - Quarantine every uncertain, cross-wired, uncited, post-2017, AGN-centered, or overbroad item. - Format: UNCITED_NOT_USABLE | candidate or claim | supplied identifier/context | exclusion reason - Explicitly quarantine claims that numerical convergence proves physical correctness, matching one tuned statistic validates a feedback mechanism, one feedback channel dominates universally, or subgrid prescriptions are first-principles predictions. - Quarantine post-2017/JWST/ML follow-up sources captured by browsing. 8. Review and source identity ledger - Repeat the review as [REV04-R00] with DOI/arXiv/ADS. - Repeat every usable primary and supporting row with author/year/journal, DOI, arXiv, ADS, role, and one-line boundary. - No source may be load-bearing unless it appears in this ledger. Quality bar - Advisory source base, not polished wiki prose. - Prefer explicit scope boundaries to broad narrative claims. - Preserve model versus observational evidence and calibrated versus predicted quantities. - Never use words such as proved, universally, exact, or definitive where the review supports only model-dependent or empirical agreement. - Ensure source keys used in findings/debates/measurements/unknowns resolve in the final usable ledger. - End with exactly: REVIEW_BASE_04_DR_COMPLETE_REFERENCE_ONLY
